hypotheses: Increasing CRPM rank to 32 and adding guide dropout at 0.1 improves held-out guide generalization by capturing more perturbation patterns while regularizing guide-specific residuals against overfitting
Enabling target-batch interaction with huber loss captures batch-specific perturbation effects while reducing sensitivity to outlier cells in pseudo-bulk aggregates

Expanding prototype flow matching capacity to condition_dim=128 and hidden_dim=384 with depth=4 and 16 inference steps improves perturbation transport modeling over the previous condition_dim=64 configuration that scored 0.6106
Doubling rank to 32 and increasing delta loss weight to 0.5 will improve mean delta Pearson by capturing more perturbation signal and focusing training on DE-relevant genes
Applying guide dropout at 0.15 during training will regularize guide-specific residuals and improve generalization to held-out guides
Learning target-specific batch response weights with interaction shrinkage 0.001 will reduce batch-confounded prediction errors for held-out guides

causal_limit: One paired nondeterministic planner sample measures direction/legality, not a numerical scientific-score treatment effect.
finding: Skill ON preserved proposal validity while avoiding the known underperforming flow-matching family proposed by Skill OFF.
